requirement:
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> {"search_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","used":["1"]}. Entries
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
rationale:
The requirement states the exact text of the `finish_search` MCP tool description, so its only structural obligation is that the tool definition carries that description.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` is marked {impl} for this requirement. It builds a `finish_search` tool definition whose `description` string matches the requirement text word for word. The only differences are JSON escaping of the example's quotation marks. Both versions cover the same points:
- Closing a delivered search and recording dependencies.
- The `search_id` and `used` explanation, with the example.
- Entries that may be omitted.
- `used:[]` for no qualifying entries.
- Every delivered search must be finished before submission.
- The `{search_id, finished:true}` result with no additional source delivered.

The definition's `parameters` schema declares `search_id` as a uuid string and `used` as an array of strings. Both are required, and additional properties are not allowed. This agrees with the description. Each definition is converted into a `ToolDefinition` through `serde_json::from_value`, so the description reaches the tool definition.

No other implementation root is needed, and the description string is the only element the requirement specifies. I found no separate test of this string. The assessment here is structural, and the requirement imposes no behavior beyond the description text. No {fixme} acknowledgments exist, and I found no structural gap.
